snippet.title: Even Coming Home Meant 30 Days of Waiting
snippet.description:
In 1377, Ragusa required arrivals from plague-affected places to wait 30 days before entering the city. The rule could apply to residents returning home, too. Later, a 40-day period gave us the word quarantine.

snippet.title: They Shared a Burrow for 250 Million Years
snippet.description:
A sleeping predator and an injured amphibian ended up in the same burrow. Their unlikely shelter became a fossil that survived for 250 million years.

This paper-diorama short tells the story of Thrinaxodon and Broomistega, two very different animals found together in an ancient South African burrow.

snippet.title: The Taj Mahal Cost Him His Hands #TajMahal #Shorts
snippet.description:
A dramatic paper-diorama retelling of the legend of Ahmad, the architect placed in charge of building the Taj Mahal—and the brutal price that followed his greatest achievement.

A short story about skill, power, and what happens when being irreplaceable becomes dangerous.
